commitResults.messageBody:
Move greeting, farewell, separators, task-list display, and task mutation messages into a dedicated Ui class. This reduces the amount of direct console-printing work inside HabpyDuck and creates a clearer boundary for later extraction of parser, storage, and task-list responsibilities.

Keep command parsing and persistence behavior unchanged in this increment so the refactor remains small and easy to verify with the existing UI test plan.

Move task file loading, saving, saved-line parsing, and field escaping into a dedicated Storage class. This gives file persistence a clear owner and keeps HabpyDuck focused on coordinating commands, UI, and task mutations.

Keep the existing data format and UI behavior unchanged, including reloading from disk when list is called. Update task serializers to depend on Storage for escaping so file-format rules stay with persistence logic.

Move command type detection, task number parsing, and user deadline date-time parsing into a dedicated Parser class. This gives command interpretation a clear owner and further reduces HabpyDuck toward an application coordinator.

Keep command handling and task mutation behavior unchanged in this increment so the refactor remains easy to verify against the existing UI transcripts.

Move task collection state behind a new TaskList class so HabpyDuck no longer manipulates ArrayList<Task> directly for add, delete, mark, unmark, reload, and size operations.

This completes the target OOP split with Ui handling console interaction, Storage handling file persistence, Parser interpreting commands, and TaskList owning task-list behavior. The UI and Storage method signatures are left stable in this increment to avoid changing console output or the save-file format while finishing the extraction.

Introduce an abstract Command type and concrete command classes for add, list, mark, unmark, delete, and exit operations. Parser now turns raw user input into command objects, including the task object for add commands and the requested task number for status and delete commands.

This removes the large command switch and command-specific helper methods from HabpyDuck, leaving the main loop responsible for reading input, parsing, executing the command, and checking whether to exit. The refactor preserves the existing console transcript and save-file behavior while making new commands easier to add later.
